notes: Handles the entire blood pressure system and application of effects.

guide.howYouGetIt: Always present (default 100). Each 2 s update it moves 20% of the way toward a target value (only ~6.7% per update when rising). Target = blood amount - Cardiac Tamponade/2 - 5 x pressure-drug (max 45) - anesthesia (max 15) + 10 x adrenaline (max 30) + 5 x saline (max 30) + 5 x Ringer's (max 30), then multiplied up by liver damage and kidney damage (up to x1.5 each at 100), alcohol withdrawal (up to x1.5), and multiplied down by traumatic shock (0 at shock 50), Irregular Heartbeat (x(100-fib)/100) and cardiac arrest (x0).
guide.whatItDoes: Low pressure (hypotension): below 60 lightheadedness + headache, below 55 blurred vision, below 50 pale skin, below 30 confusion; below 70 it drives hypoxemia up ((70-BP)/7 per second); below about 81 it speeds up Irregular Heartbeat. High pressure (hypertension) above 150: each update a heart-attack chance of (BP-150)/50 x 2% (not with streptokinase in blood or no heart) and a stroke chance of (BP-150)/50 x 2% (+5% while streptokinase is in blood). Kidneys take extra damage when BP > 120.
guide.treatment: Hypotension: stop bleeding and transfuse blood (+30 BP and restores blood), saline/Ringer's (raise target up to +30), adrenaline (+up to 30), CPR (+5/s while CPR active). Hypertension: nitroglycerin / sodium nitroprusside (Blood Pressure Reducers lowers the target by 5 per point, max 45), treat liver/kidney damage and alcohol withdrawal.
guide.naturalRecovery: Sometimes. Returns toward normal on its own once the inputs (blood amount, drugs, shock, heart rhythm) are normal.
guide.progression: Lerps toward its target every update; clamped 5-200. Does not change in stasis.

code.title: Hypoxemia
code.effects: Changes Blood Pressure, Specific Organ Damage (requires them to be Constant).

guide.howYouGetIt: Lack of oxygen in the blood. Each second it changes by (50 - available oxygen)/8. Available oxygen = the character's breathing oxygen (0-100) x (1 - Irregular Heartbeat/100), capped at 100 - pneumothorax/2, and forced to 0 during cardiac arrest, with lung damage at 100, or with lungs removed. It also rises by (70-BP)/7 per second when blood pressure is under 70 and by (60-blood)/4 per second when blood amount is under 60%. Respiratory arrest causes it indirectly via Oxygen Low. Cyanide poisoning adds it directly.
guide.whatItDoes: Neurotrauma +hypoxemia/100 per second, bone damage +hypoxemia/1000 per second, and organ damage to heart/lungs/liver/kidneys (+hypoxemia/400 per second each). Above 10 hyperventilation, above 20 shortness of breath, above 40 headache, above 50 confusion, above 70 a 5% chance per update of respiratory arrest, above 80 unconsciousness and a 1% chance per update of cardiac arrest. Above 80 it also keeps cardiac arrest from clearing; above 70 it keeps respiratory arrest from clearing; above 30 it blocks mannitol's neurotrauma healing. Raises Irregular Heartbeat speed (up to +1.5).
guide.treatment: Restore breathing (bag-valve mask removes respiratory arrest/Oxygen Low, operating table/hospital bed artificial ventilation), restore circulation (CPR, defibrillation), stop bleeding and transfuse, raise blood pressure, drain pneumothorax. Liquid oxygenite removes 100 (with organ damage side effects); deusizine reduces it.
guide.naturalRecovery: Sometimes. Recovers on its own once breathing, circulation and blood volume are restored.
guide.progression: Clamped 0-100. Recovers at up to double speed when oxygen is good, but recovery fades out as blood amount drops below 50%. Frozen in stasis.

guide.howYouGetIt: Always evaluated (formerly tachycardia). Harmless floor of 2 if sepsis > 20, blood amount < 60, acidosis > 20, pneumothorax > 30, adrenaline > 1 or alcohol withdrawal > 75. code.title: Stasis
notes: Applied via Stasis Bag item.

guide.howYouGetIt: Stasis bag worn (+3).
guide.whatItDoes: 'Stasis' stat: freezes most progression (organ damage, hypoxemia, BP, sepsis, infections, coma, stroke, neurotrauma); also sustains cardiac and respiratory arrest; counts as sedated; reduces husk infection below 100.
guide.progression: Decays 1/s; refreshed while the bag is worn.

code.title: Stasis Bag Overlay
notes: Applied via Stasis Bag item.

name: Stimulated Bone Growth
description: Bone regrowth has been stimulated. To cure Bone Death, this affliction needs to be on every bodypart.

guide.howYouGetIt: Successful osteosynthesis implant (+100 on that limb).
guide.whatItDoes: Intended to speed bone-damage healing (see Bone Damage note).

code.title: StopCreatureAbuse
notes: Used to decrease additional fall damage for certain creatures.

guide.howYouGetIt: Hypertension above 150 (chance (BP-150)/50 x 2% + 5% while streptokinase is in blood, per update, +5); streptokinase given while a stroke exists (+5).
guide.whatItDoes: Neurotrauma +0.1 x min(stroke,20) per second (max 2/s), headache, and a 5% chance per update of +14 coma and +10 seizure.
guide.treatment: Suture with the head skin retracted (>=95) removes it; mannitol to limit neurotrauma; lower blood pressure.
guide.naturalRecovery: Yes. Slowly, depends on clotting rate.
guide.progression: Clears at clotting rate/20 per second (~0.05/s; slower with liver damage or streptokinase). Frozen in stasis.

name: Sufforin Poisoning
description: Sneaky, slowly progressing poisoning that eventually leads to death.

guide.treatment: Toxin Filter on a Surgery Table treats all vanilla poisons (slower than antidotes).

name: Surgery Incision
description: An incision has been made by a Scalpel.

code.title: Surgical Incision
code.effects: Blood Loss, Traumatic Shock, increases self in XML.

guide.howYouGetIt: Advanced scalpel on a limb (removes sutures, casts, bandages there).
guide.whatItDoes: Grows 30/s. Without a clamped hemostat: +0.7 blood loss/s. Without analgesia/anesthesia while conscious: +2 traumatic shock/s.

name: Stitched Incision
description: An incision has been closed using Sutures.

guide.howYouGetIt: Suturing a surgical incision.
guide.whatItDoes: Cosmetic marker.

name: Stitched Wound
description: Wounds have been closed using Sutures.

code.title: Sutured Wound
code.effects: Vitality damage proportional to affliction strength.

guide.howYouGetIt: Suturing open wounds (amount = damage healed).
guide.whatItDoes: Up to 0.8 x max vitality loss while it fades.

name: Sweating
description: The patient is sweating excessively. Usually caused by a Heart Attack or Drug Withdrawal.

code.title: Sweating
notes: Removes itself when conditions are NOT met. Applied by other afflictions.

guide.howYouGetIt: Heart attack, alcohol withdrawal > 30.
guide.whatItDoes: Diagnostic symptom shown while the cause persists.
guide.progression: Symptom: refreshed by causes, disappears ~2 updates after.

code.title: Cardiac Tamponade
code.effects: Decreases Blood Pressure, Weakness, Cough, Shortness of Breath.
notes: Additional interaction with: Needle.

treatments.note: Requires Torso Retracted Skin >= 95; disabled by config NT_OpenCloseTamponade

guide.howYouGetIt: Blood around the heart. Gunshot to the torso hitting the heart (+5); lacerations to the torso (chance (strength-5)/50, +5).
guide.whatItDoes: Lowers blood pressure target by Cardiac Tamponade/2. Above 10 shortness of breath, above 20 cough, above 30 weakness.
guide.treatment: Chest needle (temporary), drainage tube or suture with torso skin retracted (>=95) removes it (unless the 'open/close tamponade' config is enabled).
guide.progression: Grows 0.5/s to 100; with a chest needle it shrinks ~0.5/s but not below 5. Removed if the heart is removed.

name: Third-degree Burn
description: The affected area is leathery, stiff and has lost all feeling. Infection is almost immediate and thus the onset of Sepsis is rapid. Antibiotic glue is the most rapid treatment, though Plastiseal can be used during Open / Close Surgery to replace the skin entirely.

guide.howYouGetIt: Display of 'burn' strength: burn above 50.
guide.whatItDoes: Indicator of burn severity; healed together with burns by bandages.

name: Traumatic Amputation
description: Most of the tissue of the left arm was torn off. This limb can be replaced after Sawing Bones.

code.title: Traumatic Left Arm Amputation
notes: Applied via Damage Sustained. Does nothing.

guide.howYouGetIt: Traumatic loss of the left arm: a damage hit on an already-fractured left arm can rip it off (gunshot strength/60, explosion strength/60, bite (strength-5)/60, laceration strength/60, blunt trauma > 15 strength/100, internal damage (strength-10)/60 chance).
guide.whatItDoes: Indicator only. The amputation event itself (gate) adds a fracture, an arterial cut and severe pain to that limb and drops the limb item.
guide.treatment: Reattach a limb/prosthetic item (Right Arm, Left Arm, Right Leg, Left Leg or prosthetic variants); stop the arterial bleed with a tourniquet.

name: Traumatic Shock
description: Usually occurring during unsafe surgery conditions, causing potentially lethal Hypotension. To perform safe surgery a patient must be under the effects of Analgesia and near any Bed, or be Unconscious.

code.title: Traumatic Shock
code.effects: Hypotension, Cardiac Arrest, Respiratory Arrest, Neurotrauma, Psychosis, Pain.

guide.howYouGetIt: Surgery on an awake, unsedated patient: open incision +2/s without analgesia/anesthesia and conscious; retracted skin +2/s, drilled or sawed bones +1.5/s without safe surgery while conscious; tweezers through a normal wound +5.
guide.whatItDoes: Blood pressure target x(100-2 x shock)/100 (0 at 50); Irregular Heartbeat speed +(shock-5)/40. Above 5 (conscious) shock pain and psychosis; above 30 a 20% per update respiratory arrest chance; above 40 a 10% per update cardiac arrest chance (and blocks both from clearing).
guide.treatment: Do surgery on an operating table with painkillers/anesthesia; stop operating to let it fall.
guide.progression: Decays 0.5/s, or 2/s if (sedated and on safe surgery) or anesthesia > 15. Removed by Traumatic Shock Immunity.
